A Creating GitHub Projects

How to create GitHub Projects

  1. Go to the GitHub Projects creation page
  2. Choose the "Board" or "Kanban" template
  3. Enter a project name and click "Create project"

✓ Default Status columns of the Board/Kanban template

No Status Backlog Ready In progress In review Done

Important: Rename your Status columns to match the labels configured below.

B Organization Projects URL

User Projects are not supported

Because of a GitHub API limitation, User Projects cannot use webhook-based sync.

Why:

Repository webhooks have no Projects v2 items event. That event is only available on Organization webhooks.

→ Please enter an Organization Projects URL.

Supported formats:

  • • Organization Projects: github.com/orgs/{org}/projects/{number}
  • ※ A /views/N suffix is ignored automatically
  • ※ User Projects (github.com/users/...) are not supported
-

C Label-Status mapping guide

How Projects Status maps to Issue Labels

When you move a card on the Projects board, the label with the same name as its Status is applied to the issue automatically.

Projects Status → Issue Label Description
= Ready, not started yet
= Work in progress
= Needs owner review
= Needs changes
= Work completed
= Paused
= Cancelled

Important: Projects Status column names and issue label names must match exactly. If you change a label below, rename the matching Status column in Projects too.

E Worker settings

📌 Cloudflare naming rule: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (-) only

Input is lowercased automatically. A default is generated when you enter the Projects URL.

If the name is taken at deploy time, the script lets you enter a new one.

🔐 Purpose: secret key that authenticates GitHub webhook → Cloudflare Worker requests

The wizard generates a secure random value. You can replace it with your own.

🔑 Required scopes:

  • • repo - read/write issue and PR labels
  • • project - read Projects (read:project)
Open the token page with scopes preselected

⚠️ The token is part of the command and may stay in your terminal history.
